## Investigation result

I read /home/aor_rex/Documents/12Projects/merrymen/opencode.md, traced the implementation across the web app, settings API, grant creation, worker loop, executor, and wall policy, and ran the relevant tests and type checks.

The implementation compiles, but there are several reasons auto-convert may appear not to work.

---

## Most likely runtime failure: the WETH/USDG price lookup is too strict

The worker attempts conversion here:

/home/aor_rex/Documents/12Projects/merrymen/worker/src/index.ts:4225

const price = await readPoolPrice(active.client, {
  token: CASH.WETH,
  tokenDecimals: 18,
  cash: CASH.USDG,
  cashDecimals: USDG_DECIMALS,
});


readPoolPrice() in:

/home/aor_rex/Documents/12Projects/merrymen/worker/src/venues/pool-price.ts

does all of the following:

1. Searches only the configured Uniswap V3 fee tiers.
2. Requires a pool to exist.
3. Requires positive USDG liquidity.
4. Attempts a 15-minute TWAP using observe().
5. Refuses to fall back to spot price if the TWAP is unavailable.

That is sensible for manipulation-resistant token valuation, but it is a problematic requirement for the funding converter.

A new or relatively inactive WETH/USDG pool can be perfectly usable for a swap while still failing the 15-minute TWAP requirement. In that case:

price === null


and the worker only logs:

[auto-convert] NOT converting: no WETH→USDG on-chain price ...


The conversion never starts.

The code comments explicitly acknowledge this risk:

// A brand-new pool has observation cardinality 1, so observe() over any real
// window reverts. That is a legitimate "no TWAP yet", not an error


This is likely the biggest practical issue. Auto-convert needs an execution quote, while readPoolPrice() is primarily a safety/valuation oracle.

### Recommended fix

Create a dedicated WETH/USDG execution quote function rather than reusing the general asset valuation function.

It should:

- Find the best WETH/USDG pool.
- Read current pool state.
- Calculate a spot quote or use a working Quoter path.
- Apply a liquidity and price-impact safety check.
- Use the resulting fee and minimum output for exactInputSingle.

The generic readPoolPrice() should remain TWAP-focused for valuation.

---

## Critical logic issue: the worker only attempts conversion when cash is below idleFloorUsdg

The conversion condition is:

if (surplusEth > 0n && cash6 < idleFloor && active.executor) {


where:

const idleFloor = BigInt(
  Math.round((cfg.idleFloorUsdg ?? 50) * 1e6)
);


This means auto-convert does not convert surplus ETH once the account has at least the configured idle floor of USDG.

That may be intentional, but it does not match the UI wording:

> “surplus ETH → USDG, gas kept”

An owner can fund the account with ETH while it already has, for example, 50 USDG or more, and observe no conversion at all. The implementation interprets auto-convert as:

> Convert ETH only when USDG cash is below the idle floor.

The UI does not explain that restriction.

### Recommended fix

Either:

- remove the cash6 < idleFloor condition and convert whenever there is surplus ETH, or
- rename/document the setting as a minimum-cash trigger, for example:

Convert ETH only when USDG cash is below this amount


At minimum, the diagnostic message should clearly say the conversion was skipped because cash is already above the threshold.

---

## Existing grants must be re-signed

The worker intentionally refuses old grants:

if (!grantHasNativeSwap(active.grant)) {
  ...
  "auto-convert is on but this key was signed before the ETH→USDG permission existed — re-sign at /grant ..."
}


This is correct behavior.

The feature marker is added to newly-created grants in:

/home/aor_rex/Documents/12Projects/merrymen/web/src/lib/session.ts

However, an existing grant stored in browser local storage will not gain the marker automatically. Turning on auto-convert in Settings is therefore insufficient.

The user must:

1. Open /grant.
2. Create/sign a new grant.
3. Replace the currently armed grant.
4. Ensure the new grant contains native-swap.

The UI does display this warning on the grant page, but the Settings page does not make the re-sign requirement prominent.

---

## The one-hour cooldown can make testing misleading

The worker has:

const AUTO_CONVERT_COOLDOWN_MS = 3_600_000;


and only updates lastAutoConvertAt after a successful executor call.

A successful conversion therefore prevents another conversion attempt for one hour. This timestamp is held only in memory, so restarting the worker resets it.

For debugging, it would be useful to expose the last attempt/success time in the dashboard or temporarily lower the interval in development.

---

## Auto-convert only runs on the live trading path

The outer condition requires:

cfg.autoConvertEnabled &&
active &&
chainCanTrade() &&
!paperActive() &&
lastGasWei !== null


Therefore it will not run when:

- the agent is in paper mode;
- the grant is on the wrong chain;
- there is no active grant;
- the executor is unavailable;
- the worker has not successfully read the ETH balance;
- the account has no bundler/executor configured.

The paper-mode deadlock was addressed correctly with readsAsBroke(), and the focused tests confirm that an account with ETH but zero USDG is no longer incorrectly classified as broke.

However, the conversion itself still requires a live executor and bundler.

---

## The reserve calculation frequently prevents small deposits from converting

The worker reserves the larger of:

const pctReserve = (lastGasWei * pct) / 100n;
const opFloor = gasPrice * 400_000n;
const reserve = pctReserve > opFloor ? pctReserve : opFloor;
const surplusEth = lastGasWei > reserve ? lastGasWei - reserve : 0n;


So even with a 1% reserve setting, the account must have more than approximately:

400,000 × current gas price


in ETH before conversion occurs.

This is deliberate and protects the account from becoming unable to submit future operations. But small deposits may produce:

surplusEth === 0n


and nothing happens.

The diagnostic log is only emitted for 180 seconds after a balance change, so if the owner checks later there may be no visible explanation.

---

## Important accounting bug after a successful conversion

After executing the conversion, the worker manually writes:

await addTrade({
  kind: "swap",
  target: CASH.WETH,
  sell_token: "ETH",
  buy_token: CASH.USDG,
  amount_usdg: usdgNum(expect6),
  status: "landed",
  ...
});


This records the conversion as landed immediately after executor.execute() returns, but it does not use the actual swap event output from the receipt.

The executor returns logs:

ExecutionResult.logs


and the repository already treats emitted logs as the authoritative source for actual fills. The converter currently records the estimated amount:

amount_usdg: usdgNum(expect6)


rather than the actual USDG received.

This will not prevent the conversion itself, but it can make the dashboard, P&L, and ledger disagree with the real balance.

No—you should not need to create another wallet.

The old wallet/account can still be used. What needs to be replaced is the grant/session key, not the smart-account wallet or its funds.

## Why the old grant cannot be used

The auto-converter sends a UserOperation containing:

ETH → SwapRouter02


That operation carries native ETH as msg.value.

The previous permission wall was created before native ETH swaps were supported. Its router permission effectively allowed:

valueLimit = 0


So the old session key could call the router only without attaching ETH. An ETH conversion would be rejected by the on-chain wall.

The new wall adds:

valueLimit > 0
tokenIn = WETH
tokenOut = allowlisted asset
recipient = the smart account itself


This is why the grant includes the new marker:

native-swap


That marker tells the worker that the currently stored grant contains the required permission.

## What you need to do

You can keep the same:

- Browser wallet
- Owner key
- Smart-account address
- ETH/USDG funds

Do this:

1. Open /grant.
2. Use the existing owner key/account.
3. Create/sign a new grant.
4. Confirm the page says the ETH → USDG permission is granted.
5. Arm/store the new grant.
6. Leave the funds in the same smart account.
7. Enable auto-convert and test with a small amount.

The smart-account address should remain the same because it is derived from the owner key. The new session key only changes the permissions used by the worker.

## Important distinction

| Item | Replace? |
|---|---:|
| Browser wallet | No |
| Owner key | No |
| Smart-account wallet | No |
| Smart-account address | No |
| Funds | No |
| Session/grant key | Yes |
| On-chain permission wall | Yes, through the new grant |

## Why the grant must be re-signed

The wall is enforced on-chain. The worker cannot add permissions after the grant has been signed. Allowing the worker to “upgrade” an old grant would defeat the purpose of the permission system.

So the correct migration is:

same owner + same smart account + new session grant


One caveat: if the current implementation does not preserve the existing smart-account grant when creating the new one, stop before submitting anything and verify the preview address on /grant. The preview address should match the existing account exactly.

## Suggested PR description

### Summary

Adds an opt-in auto-conversion flow that allows an agent account funded with native ETH to convert surplus ETH into USDG while preserving a gas reserve.

The flow uses the existing session-key permission wall and does not require creating a new smart account or moving funds.

### What changed

#### Settings and UI

- Added an autoConvertEnabled setting, disabled by default.
- Added configurable autoConvertReservePct with a 1–50% range.
- Added auto-convert controls to /settings.
- Updated onboarding and grant-page copy to explain that ETH can be converted into USDG.
- Added validation and persistence through the settings API.

#### Permission wall and grants

- Added the native-swap grant capability marker.
- Extended the SwapRouter02 permission to support bounded native ETH value.
- Keeps the swap constrained by:
- Allowlisted token inputs and outputs.
- The agent account as the recipient.
- A sealed per-operation native value limit.
- Existing grant expiry and session-key restrictions.
- Newly-created grants include the native-swap capability.
- Older grants remain intentionally incompatible and must be re-signed.

#### Worker execution

- Added native ETH → USDG conversion call construction using exactInputSingle.
- Sends ETH as msg.value and uses WETH as the router’s input token.
- Preserves an operator gas reserve before calculating the convertible surplus.
- Limits automatic conversions to one attempt per hour.
- Prevents conversion while the account is in paper mode.
- Correctly treats an account with ETH but zero USDG as funded, avoiding the previous paper-mode deadlock.
- Adds diagnostic logging and event messages for skipped conversions and stale grants.

#### Safety and correctness

- Keeps conversion recipient pinned to the agent’s own account.
- Does not grant arbitrary ETH transfers.
- Does not add withdrawal permissions.
- Does not widen the existing asset allowlist.
- Leaves general portfolio valuation on the stricter TWAP-based pricing path.

### Testing

- Added tests for:
- Native swap call construction.
- Native-swap grant capability detection.
- Wall value limits and calldata restrictions.
- ETH-funded accounts with zero USDG.
- Updated the paper-mode regression test.
- Full test suite passes: 1,584 tests
- Typecheck passes.
- Production build passes.

### User migration

Existing users do not need a new wallet or smart account.

To enable auto-convert on an existing account:

1. Open /grant.
2. Re-sign the grant using the existing owner key.
3. Confirm the smart-account address is unchanged.
4. Confirm the ETH → USDG permission is shown as granted.
5. Enable auto-convert in Settings.

The new grant is required because the old on-chain wall was created with a zero native-value limit and cannot be upgraded after signing.

### Known behavior

- Auto-convert is disabled by default.
- It requires a live executor and bundler.
- It only runs on the supported live trading chain.
- It preserves a dynamic gas reserve.
- Automatic conversion is rate-limited to once per hour.
- Auto-convert currently targets SwapRouter02/Uniswap.

Add guarded native ETH → USDG auto-conversion

## PR description

### Summary

Adds an opt-in auto-conversion flow for funded Merrymen agent accounts.

When enabled, surplus native ETH is converted to USDG through Uniswap’s SwapRouter02, while retaining a configurable percentage of the account’s ETH for gas. The conversion is executed by the existing session-key/bundler flow and remains constrained by the on-chain permission wall.

This uses the existing smart account and owner key. Users do not need to create a new wallet or move their funds.

### What changed

#### Settings and onboarding

- Added autoConvertEnabled, disabled by default.
- Added autoConvertReservePct, configurable from 1–50%.
- Added Settings UI controls for enabling auto-conversion and configuring the reserve percentage.
- Updated onboarding and grant-page copy to explain ETH funding and automatic USDG conversion.
- Added settings API validation and persistence.
- Added worker-side settings resolution and clamping.

#### Native swap permission

- Added the native-swap grant capability marker.
- Extended the SwapRouter02 permission to support bounded native ETH value.
- Allows native ETH only through the approved exactInputSingle route.
- Keeps the following restrictions:
- Token input and output remain restricted to the grant’s allowlisted assets.
- The recipient remains pinned to the agent’s own smart account.
- Native value is bounded by a sealed per-operation limit.
- Existing grant expiry and session-key restrictions remain active.
- Older grants are not silently upgraded and must be re-signed before they can perform native ETH conversions.

#### Worker conversion flow

- Added native ETH → USDG call construction.
- Uses WETH as the router input token and sends native ETH through msg.value.
- Preserves a gas reserve before calculating the convertible ETH surplus.
- Limits automatic conversion to one successful conversion per hour.
- Runs only for live, funded accounts with an active executor.
- Avoids the previous paper-mode deadlock where an account with ETH but zero USDG was incorrectly treated as unfunded.
- Adds diagnostics for skipped conversions and stale grants.

#### Execution pricing

- Added a dedicated execution-price path for WETH/USDG.
- Prefers the 15-minute TWAP when available.
- Falls back to the current pool spot price when a TWAP is unavailable, such as for a newly initialized pool.
- Keeps the existing TWAP-only behavior for portfolio valuation and safety decisions.

### Security considerations

The native swap permission is intentionally narrow:

- Only the configured SwapRouter02 target is permitted.
- The native ETH amount is capped per operation.
- The swap input/output assets are allowlisted.
- The recipient is pinned to the smart account itself.
- No arbitrary native ETH transfer permission is added.
- No withdrawal permission is added.
- Auto-convert is opt-in and disabled by default.

### User migration

Existing users can keep their current:

- Browser wallet
- Owner key
- Smart account
- Smart-account address
- Existing funds

4. Confirm that the ETH → USDG permission is shown as granted.
5. Enable auto-convert in Settings.
6. Fund the existing smart account with a small test amount.

### Known limitations

- Auto-convert is disabled by default.
- It currently targets Uniswap SwapRouter02.
- It requires a live executor and configured bundler.
- It only runs on the supported live trading chain.
- The conversion is rate-limited to one successful operation per hour.
- A dynamic gas reserve is always retained.
- Execution spot fallback is used only for the conversion quote; portfolio valuation remains TWAP-based.

### Testing

- Added native conversion call-construction tests.
- Added grant capability and wall-policy tests.
- Added funded-with-ETH/zero-USDG regression coverage.
- Added execution quote fallback support.

# Add guarded native ETH → USDG auto-conversion

## Summary

This PR adds an opt-in auto-conversion flow for Merrymen agent accounts.

When enabled, an account funded with native ETH can automatically convert its surplus ETH into USDG through Uniswap’s SwapRouter02, while keeping enough ETH available for future gas costs.

The feature uses the existing smart account, owner key, session key, and bundler flow. Users do not need to create a new wallet or move existing funds.

## What changed

### Settings and onboarding

- Added autoConvertEnabled, disabled by default.
- Added autoConvertReservePct, configurable between 1% and 50%.
- Added auto-conversion controls to the Settings page.
- Added validation and persistence through the Settings API.
- Updated onboarding and grant-page copy to explain ETH funding and automatic USDG conversion.
- Added worker-side settings resolution and clamping.

### Native swap permission

The permission wall now supports a narrowly-scoped native ETH swap capability.

- Added the native-swap grant marker.
- Extended the SwapRouter02 permission to support bounded native ETH value.
- Restricts the swap to the approved exactInputSingle entrypoint.
- Restricts input and output tokens to the grant’s allowlisted assets.
- Pins the recipient to the agent’s own smart account.
- Applies a sealed per-operation native ETH limit.
- Preserves the existing grant expiry and session-key restrictions.
- Does not add arbitrary ETH transfer or withdrawal permissions.

Older grants cannot be upgraded automatically. Grants created before this capability was introduced must be re-signed before auto-conversion can be used.

### Worker execution

The worker now performs the conversion on the live execution path.

- Builds a native ETH → USDG exactInputSingle call.
- Uses WETH as the router input token.
- Sends native ETH through msg.value.
- Keeps a dynamic gas reserve before calculating the convertible surplus.
- Limits successful automatic conversions to one per hour.
- Runs only for live accounts with an active executor.
- Prevents paper mode from blocking conversion when an account has ETH but no USDG.
- Emits diagnostic messages when conversion is skipped.

### Execution pricing

Auto-conversion now has a dedicated WETH/USDG execution-price path.

- Uses the 15-minute TWAP when it is available.
- Falls back to the pool’s current spot price when a TWAP is not yet available.
- Supports newly initialized pools that do not have enough observation history.
- Keeps the existing TWAP-only behavior for portfolio valuation and safety checks.

The spot-price fallback is used only to construct the execution quote. It does not change how portfolio value, P&L, or safety decisions are calculated.

## Safety model

The native swap remains constrained by the on-chain permission wall:

- Target: approved SwapRouter02 contract only.
- Entrypoint: exactInputSingle only.
- Input token: allowlisted assets, including WETH for native ETH conversion.
- Output token: allowlisted assets.
- Recipient: the agent’s own smart account.
- Native value: bounded by a sealed per-operation limit.
- Default state: disabled.
- Withdrawals: not permitted.
- Arbitrary ETH transfers: not permitted.

The conversion flow does not bypass the existing wall. The submitted UserOperation is still checked by the account’s on-chain permissions.

## Existing-user migration

Existing users do not need to create a new wallet or smart account.

They can keep their:

- Existing browser wallet.
- Existing owner key.
- Existing smart-account address.
- Existing ETH and USDG balances.

However, they must create a new grant because the previous grant was signed before native ETH swaps were supported.

### Migration steps

1. Open /grant.
2. Re-sign the grant using the existing owner key.
3. Confirm that the preview smart-account address matches the existing account.
4. Confirm that the ETH → USDG permission is shown as granted.
5. Enable auto-conversion in Settings.
6. Test with a small ETH deposit.

The new grant changes the session permissions, not the smart-account wallet or its funds.

## Known limitations

- Auto-conversion is disabled by default.
- The current implementation targets Uniswap SwapRouter02.
- A live executor and configured bundler are required.
- Conversion runs only on the supported live trading chain.
- Successful conversions are rate-limited to one per hour.
- A gas reserve is always retained.
- Auto-conversion uses the execution quote path; portfolio valuation remains TWAP-based.
- The actual conversion is still subject to pool liquidity, slippage, and the on-chain permission wall.

## Testing

Added and updated coverage for:

- Native ETH conversion call construction.
- Native swap grant capability detection.
- Swap wall value limits.
- Token and recipient restrictions.
- ETH-funded accounts with zero USDG.
- Spot-price fallback when TWAP data is unavailable.
- Paper-mode behavior.
- Settings and worker integration paths.

## How to test auto-convert

### 1. Update to the latest branch

cd /home/aor_rex/Documents/12Projects/merrymen
git checkout dev/auto-convert
git pull origin dev/auto-convert
npm install


### 2. Start the web app and worker

In terminal 1:

cd /home/aor_rex/Documents/12Projects/merrymen
npm run dev:web


In terminal 2:

cd /home/aor_rex/Documents/12Projects/merrymen
npm run dev:worker


The worker needs:

- A valid RPC endpoint.
- A configured Pimlico bundler URL/API key.
- The existing owner/grant data.
- A funded smart account.

Run:

npm run doctor


to check the local setup.

### 3. Re-sign the grant

You do not need a new wallet.

1. Open the web app’s /grant page.
2. Use the existing owner key/account.
3. Create a new grant.
4. Confirm the preview smart-account address matches the existing address.
5. Confirm the page says:

ETH → USDG — granted


6. Arm/save the new grant.

This step is required because old grants were signed before the native ETH swap permission existed.

### 4. Enable auto-convert

Open /settings and:

1. Enable Fund with ETH — auto-convert to USDG.
2. Leave the reserve at the default 10% initially.
3. Save the settings.

Verify the setting was stored:

cat ~/.merrymen/settings.json


You should see:

{
  "autoConvertEnabled": true,
  "autoConvertReservePct": 10
}


If your installation uses a custom data directory, use the settings path reported by:

npm run doctor


### 5. Fund the existing smart account

Copy the smart-account address from /grant or /app.

Send a small but meaningful amount of native ETH on the supported live chain to that address.

Do not test with an amount that is barely enough for gas. The worker keeps a gas reserve:

max(percentage reserve, estimated one-operation gas reserve)


For an initial test, use an amount comfortably above that reserve. You can reduce the amount after confirming the flow works.

Do not send ETH to:

- The owner wallet, unless that wallet is also the smart account.
- The bundler address.
- The router address.

Send it to the smart-account address.

### 6. Watch the worker logs

After the ETH deposit is visible on-chain, watch the worker terminal.

A successful conversion should look similar to:

[auto-convert] 0.00... ETH → ~... USDG (min ...) · op 0x...


The event feed should also contain:

auto-convert ✓ ... ETH → ~... USDG


The worker may wait until the next tick. The default tick interval is controlled by tickSeconds.

### 7. Confirm the result on-chain

Verify all of the following:

- ETH balance decreased, but a gas reserve remains.
- USDG balance increased.
- The recipient of the USDG is the smart-account address.
- The operation’s UserOperation hash appears in the logs.
- The transaction succeeded on the chain explorer.
- The event/trade appears in the Merrymen dashboard.

The conversion is limited to one successful operation per hour, so do not expect another conversion immediately after the first one.

## If it does not convert

Check the worker logs for one of these messages.

### Old grant

auto-convert is on but this key was signed before the ETH→USDG permission existed


Fix: re-sign the grant at /grant.

### No usable pool

no WETH→USDG on-chain price


Possible causes:

- Wrong network.
- No WETH/USDG pool found.
- RPC is pointed at the wrong chain.
- Pool has no usable spot price.
- The account is not using the supported live chain.

### Not enough surplus ETH

surplus ... ETH is not above the gas reserve


Fix: fund the smart account with more ETH. The worker intentionally will not spend the amount needed for future gas.

### Paper mode or no executor

If there is no conversion log at all, check:

- The grant is on the supported live chain.
- A bundler URL/API key is configured.
- The worker has armed the grant.
- The account is not in paper mode.
- autoConvertEnabled is actually true.
- The ETH balance read succeeded.

Run:

npm run doctor
npm run status


## Local automated validation

Before testing with real funds:

npm test
npm run typecheck
npm run build


Expected result:

1,584 tests passed


These checks validate the conversion call, permission wall, grant marker, paper-mode boundary, and pricing fallback. They do not replace a live on-chain test.

## Recommended first live test

Use this sequence:

1. Existing smart account.
2. Freshly re-signed grant.
3. Auto-convert enabled.
4. Reserve percentage: 10%.
5. Small ETH deposit with a comfortable amount above gas requirements.
6. Worker logs open.
7. Confirm one successful conversion.
8. Wait at least one hour before testing another automatic conversion.

how will i know the key has been signed
A
Assistant openai/gpt-5.6-luna
You can confirm it in three ways.

## 1. Check the /grant page

After you sign with your existing owner key, the page should complete the grant flow and show the grant details.

Look for:

ETH → USDG — granted


The page should also show:

- The smart-account address.
- The owner address.
- The session/grant expiry.
- The enabled capabilities.
- A success/armed state after saving.

Most importantly, confirm that the displayed smart-account address is the same address as before.

## 2. Check the worker logs

After the new grant is saved, the worker should re-read it and arm the account. Look for a message indicating that the grant was armed or synchronized.

Then, if you enable auto-convert, an old grant should no longer produce:

auto-convert is on but this key was signed before the ETH→USDG permission existed


Instead, once the account is funded and eligible, it should attempt the conversion.

## 3. Check the stored grant directly

The grant is normally stored in the browser’s localStorage, not in the worker settings file.

Open your browser’s Developer Tools:

1. Go to Application or Storage.
2. Select Local Storage for your Merrymen site.
3. Find the grant entry, usually beginning with something like:

merrymen.grant


4. Inspect the JSON value.

Look for a grantFeatures array containing:

"native-swap"


You should also see the same smartAccount address as before.

Do not paste or share the complete stored grant. It may contain private/session key material.

## What successful signing means

There are two separate signatures involved:

1. Owner-key signature
This proves the generated grant is authorized by the owner key.

2. Wallet signature
This authenticates the browser wallet/session where required.

You do not need to inspect the raw signature. If the grant page accepts the signatures, stores the grant, and displays native-swap as granted, the grant was signed successfully.

## Important distinction

The grant itself is not a normal standalone blockchain transaction. You should not expect:

- A gas charge.
- A transaction hash.
- A block explorer transaction.
- An on-chain “grant signed” event.

The permission is encoded in the grant and enforced when the session key later submits a UserOperation.

The clearest confirmation is:

/grant shows ETH → USDG: granted
+ smart-account address is unchanged
+ stored grantFeatures contains "native-swap"


Only after those checks should you enable auto-convert and fund the account.

You’re right — based on the files and timestamps, this is not you alternating accounts manually. The application is allowing a second account to become active when you click the grant/recovery controls.

## What happened

Your worker log showed:

0xa48c... · eth 0.000947...
0x0d09... · eth 0
0xa48c... · eth 0
0xa48c... · cash 1000 USDG


Those are genuinely different smart accounts.

The stored files show:

/home/aor_rex/.merrymen/grant.json
→ 0xa48cE91e2F3237E69660C1543042c007B8D33e75
→ owner 0x8429...
→ chain 4663
→ native-swap


That is your funded account.

The second account is:

0x0d095153f44cDBc78377eA5d88965dF58Eb573f1
→ owner 0xf124...
→ chain 4663
→ native-swap


It was written at approximately 12:25, while the correct account was written again at approximately 12:29.

So the UI created or restored a different account, posted it to the single active grant file, and the worker correctly followed the file. Then the correct account was posted again later.

## Why this can happen

The /grant page has two separate flows:

- Create your agent — generates a brand-new owner key and therefore a brand-new smart account.
- Restore an existing wallet — derives an account from a recovery key.

The application archives old grants, but the worker only reads:

/home/aor_rex/.merrymen/grant.json


The archive directory is not an account selector for the worker.

The dangerous UX bug is that clicking the wrong grant action can replace the active grant immediately. The application does archive the previous grant, so your old funds are not moved, but the worker can temporarily run against the wrong empty account.

## Your current funded account is safe

The current active file is again:

0xa48cE91e2F3237E69660C1543042c007B8D33e75


It contains:

"grantFeatures": [
  "tradeable-v2",
  "native-swap"
]


So the native swap permission is present, and the account is correctly prepared.

Do not create another wallet and do not fund 0x0d095....

## What should be fixed

The grant page needs a safer “renew/re-sign” flow:

1. When a grant already exists, disable or hide Create your agent.
2. Make Restore existing wallet the primary action.
3. Require the recovery key preview to match the currently funded account before allowing submission.
4. Show a blocking warning if the preview address differs from the active funded account.
5. Require explicit confirmation before replacing the active grant with a different smart account.
6. Prevent a failed or incomplete grant operation from changing the active grant.
7. Make the worker log the owner, chain, and grant file timestamp when it re-arms, so this cannot appear mysterious.

The current code archives the old grant, which protects the key material, but it does not prevent accidental active-account replacement.

## What to do right now

1. Stop clicking the grant buttons.
2. Keep the active file as the funded account:

0xa48cE91e2F3237E69660C1543042c007B8D33e75


3. Restart the worker once:

Ctrl+C
   npm start


4. Confirm every worker cycle reports the same address.
5. Only then test auto-convert.

Your current logs also show:

autoConvertEnabled: true
native-swap: present
executor live


The missing piece is that the active account was being replaced underneath the worker.

The next code change should be the active-account replacement guard, not another wallet or another grant.

## The next code fix

The executor needs a bounded timeout and a durable in-flight lock.

### 1. Add an execution timeout

The conversion should fail with a visible error after a fixed period, for example:

## The real math (this is the review)

The EntryPoint's prefund requirement for an undeployed account is:

prefund = (verificationGasLimit × 3 + callGasLimit + preVerificationGas) × maxFeePerGas


Three multipliers because the account isn't deployed yet. With the executor's 2× headroom applied to every field, realistic estimates for Kernel deployment + permission-validator init + SwapRouter02 swap are:

| Field | Bundler estimate | ×2 headroom |
|---|---:|---:|
| verificationGasLimit (deploy + validate) | ~250–400k | 500–800k, ×3 = 1.5–2.4M |
| callGasLimit (factory + swap) | ~250–400k | 500–800k |
| preVerificationGas | ~50k | ~100k |
| Prefund total | | ~2.1–3.3M gas |

At maxFeePerGas = 0.704 gwei:

prefund ≈ 2.1–3.3M × 0.704 gwei ≈ 0.0015–0.0023 ETH


Your actual numbers this run:

balance:        0.0044949 ETH
swap value:     0.0039327 ETH   ← 87.5% of balance
left for gas:   0.0005622 ETH   ← needs ~0.0015–0.0023 → FAILS


My 1,000,000 gas floor computes 0.000562 ETH — almost exactly what was left, and roughly 3× short of the true undeployed prefund. The reserve must be gasPrice × ~2,500,000 for a first operation.

## The fix (planned, not yet applied)

In worker/src/index.ts, change:

const opFloor = gasPrice * (deployed ? 600_000n : 1_000_000n);


to:

// EntryPoint prefund = (verification×3 + call + preVerification) × maxFee,
// all at 2x headroom. Deployed: ~1.2M gas. Undeployed first op adds
// deployment and counts verification ×3: ~2.5M gas. Sizing the floor
// below this is how AA21 keeps recurring on small balances.
const opFloor = gasPrice * (deployed ? 1_200_000n : 2_500_000n);


Effect on your balance:

reserve  = 0.562 gwei × 2.5M ≈ 0.001405 ETH
surplus  = 0.0044949 − 0.001405 ≈ 0.00309 ETH ≈ 7.6 USDG
left after swap = 0.0014 ETH ≥ prefund requirement → simulation passes


After the first successful operation the account is deployed, and subsequent converts use the smaller 1.2M floor — so the reserve shrinks on every later convert.

## Trade-off to be aware of

On small deposits the converter converts less (≈69% instead of 90%). That is correct behavior — the alternative is the bundler refusing every attempt, as it has been. The autoConvertReservePct percentage only ever *raises* the reserve above this floor, never lowers it.

Still AA21 "didn't pay prefund" — the reserve floor is still under what the bundler's simulation demands. Here's the honest read of the numbers.

## Where we are now

balance:   0.0044949 ETH
swap:      0.0030649 ETH  (msg.value, leaves in the same op)
left:      0.0014300 ETH  ← what the prefund must fit in
required:  apparently MORE than 0.00143 ETH at ~0.71 gwei maxFee


So the undeployed-first-op prefund is greater than ~2.0M gas — my 2.5M-gas estimate at the *bundler's* fee (0.71 gwei, not the raw 0.57) is still short. The likely breakdown:

verificationGasLimit (deployment + validators): ~500–700k ×2 headroom ×3 = 3.0–4.2M
callGasLimit (swap):                            ~400–500k ×2            = 0.8–1.0M
preVerificationGas:                             ~80k ×2                 = 0.16M
total: ~4.0–5.4M gas × 0.71 gwei ≈ 0.0028–0.0038 ETH


My formula underestimated how heavily the ×3 multiplier and 2× headroom compound on the deployment verification.

## The plan (two parts)

### 1. Stop guessing — size the floor from the failure itself

Raise the undeployed floor to 5,000,000 gas and the deployed floor to 2,000,000 gas:

reserve  = 0.57 gwei × 5M ≈ 0.00286 ETH
surplus  = 0.0044949 − 0.00286 ≈ 0.00163 ETH → ~4.0 USDG converted
left over = 0.00286 ETH ≥ required ~0.0028–0.0038 → borderline but plausible


To be safe on the *first* attempt, I'd also cap the surplus so the leftover is max(floor, 15% of balance) — belt and braces for the deployment op.

### 2. The cleaner alternative — deploy first, convert second

Instead of one mega-op, the worker could submit a trivial deployment-only UserOp (a 0-value self-call) once, then run the convert as a normal deployed-account op with the small 2M floor. That is:

- More reliable (no compound ×3 deployment math).
- Wastes one small op's gas (~0.0002–0.0004 ETH) once, ever.
- Leaves auto-convert itself simple.

## My recommendation

Do both: raise the floors now (immediate unblock), and add a one-time pre-deploy op so all future converts run with the modest deployed-account floor. On small deposits the converter will move less per pass (~4 USDG on yours) — that is the correct cost of self-deploying safely; it gets cheaper after deployment.

Committed and pushed.

### Commit

7424a6f fix: deploy the account with a dust approve before converting


### What this change does

Instead of trying to squeeze deployment into the convert operation (which kept failing AA21 no matter how the floor was tuned), auto-convert now works in two steps:

Step 1 — deploy first. If getCode() shows the smart account is undeployed, the worker submits a *policy-legal dust op*: USDG.approve(SwapRouter02, 1n) — 0.000001 USDG of allowance, the same no-op the selftest uses. This deploys the Kernel account and initializes the permission validator through the normal factory path, without needing the ×3 prefund of a value-carrying op.

Step 2 — convert as a deployed account. The convert then runs with the modest 2M-gas prefund floor instead of the impossible undeployed math.

Also in this commit:

- Floors: deployed = gasPrice × 2M, undeployed fallback = gasPrice × 5M (only if the probe path can't run).
- The duplicated timeout/in-flight logic is now one shared autoConvertExecute() helper used by both the probe and the convert — same 120s bound, same duplicate-submission guard, same onSubmitted logging.
- A failing deploy probe sets the cooldown clock so a persistent refusal retries hourly instead of spamming every tick.

### Validation

- Full suite: 1,584 tests passed, 0 failed
- Worker typecheck: passed
- git diff --check: passed

### Test it

npm start

## Why

For an undeployed account the EntryPoint multiplies verification gas by 3. Kernel v3.3 deployment + session-key validator + call-policy enable is expensive to verify — roughly 2M gas, so:

prefund ≈ (2M × 3 + call + preVerification) × 0.71 gwei
        ≈ 6.2M gas × 0.71 gwei
        ≈ 0.0044 ETH

happens once and converts are cheap afterward.

You've hit the real product flaw, and the honest answer is: yes, today a small first deposit can't auto-convert — and that's a design gap worth fixing, not just explaining.

## Why it happens

The smart account is *counterfactual*: it has an address but no code until its first UserOperation pays to deploy it. Deployment (~2M verification gas ×3 ≈ 0.0045 ETH at current prices) is a fixed one-time cost, independent of deposit size. A $20 deposit and a $20,000 deposit pay the same deployment bill — but only the big one has enough left over to pay it. So small first deposits are stranded: the money is on-chain, but the account can't act yet.

The session-key wall makes no difference here — this is pure ERC-4337 mechanics.

## How this should be solved (design options)

### Option A — sponsor the deployment op (best; infra already exists)

The repo already has full paymaster sponsorship (worker/src/paymaster.ts, createSponsor, the sponsorGasEnabled setting, and the hosted house paymaster). A sponsored op doesn't need the account to prefund — the paymaster's deposit covers gas. So:

- If a sponsor is configured (always true on hosted; optional self-hosted), send the deploy probe sponsored → deployment works at any deposit size.
- Self-hosted without a paymaster: fall back to the current behavior plus the clear "needs ~0.005 ETH to deploy" message.

This makes auto-convert work for *any* first deposit on hosted, which is where most users are.

### Option B — document a minimum first funding

Simplest but weakest: state "first deposit should be ≥ ~0.006 ETH" in the onboarding fund step. Doesn't fix the strand — just warns before it happens.

### Option C — owner-key escape hatch

The owner key (sudo) can also deploy the account via a UserOp funded from... the same balance, so no help. (Recover sweeps, doesn't deploy-and-keep.) Not a real option.

## Recommended plan

1. Sponsor the deploy probe when a sponsor is available — the executor already accepts a sponsor; the probe is a policy-legal op, and the paymaster settles with the EntryPoint directly. Deposit size stops mattering for deployment.
2. Add the pre-check event from before: if no sponsor and balance < undeployed floor, emit the precise "needs ~X ETH one-time deployment" message instead of attempting and failing hourly.
3. Surface it in the UI copy: fund step says "first deposit deploys your account (~0.005 ETH of gas, once); after that, any amount works."

Deployment is one-time, so after it succeeds every later deposit — however small — converts normally.

Here's the user journey with the code as it now stands (all pushed):

## User A — first deposit ≥ ~0.01 ETH

Everything works automatically.

1. Deposit lands → next tick, worker logs account undeployed — sending a dust approve first to deploy it.
2. Deploy op pays ~0.0045 ETH of gas once.
3. Convert runs immediately after with the cheap deployed-account floor (~0.0011 ETH reserve at current gas).
4. On a 0.01 ETH deposit: roughly 0.004 ETH converts to ~10 USDG, ~0.005 stays as working reserve.

From then on the account is deployed forever — every future deposit of *any* size converts normally, down to tiny amounts. The fixed cost is paid once, at the start.

## User B — first deposit < ~0.005 ETH

Their money is safe but stranded until they top up.

1. Convert attempts fail AA21 ("didn't pay prefund") — the bundler refuses to even quote, nothing is broadcast, no gas is lost. Retries hourly, fails identically each time.
2. The funds sit untouched in the smart account. Nothing is lost; the owner key can always recover them via merrymen recover.
3. The moment their cumulative balance crosses ~0.0046 ETH, the next tick deploys the account and auto-convert starts working — including converting the original small deposit.

So it's not "small deposits can never convert" — it's "the account needs ~0.005 ETH total before the first conversion can happen." A user who sends 0.002 then 0.004 later is fine; a user who sends 0.002 and stops is stuck.

## That's the gap

The current UX tells User B nothing actionable — the event says "gas refused," which reads like a bug, not "send a bit more." That's bad.

## The two fixes, in priority order

1. No-code UX fix (small, safe): pre-check the balance against the deployment floor and emit a plain-language event:
> "Your account needs ~0.0003 more ETH to pay its one-time setup cost. Top up the smart account and auto-convert will start on its own."

2. Real fix (bigger): sponsor the deploy op via the existing paymaster when one is configured — hosted users (the majority) then work at *any* deposit size, and self-hosters get it free if they enable sponsorGasEnabled with a Pimlico policy.

## What was implemented (local, worker/src/index.ts, +38/−5)

The auto-convert path is now sponsor-aware via the existing gasSponsored() (sponsorGasEnabled && bundlerApiKey — the executor is already built with the paymaster when that's on):

1. Deployment pre-check is sponsor-aware.

- Sponsored: skips the balance gate entirely — the paymaster pays the deployment gas from its own deposit, so AA21 can't fire on a small balance. Logs: deployment is gas-sponsored, deploying at any balance.
- Unsponsored: keeps the clear pre-check ("needs ~X ETH one-time setup") from the previous change.

2. Reserve shrinks when sponsored.

## How to enable gas sponsorship

### Step 1 — Create a Pimlico sponsorship policy

1. Go to https://dashboard.pimlico.io and sign in with the account that owns your API key (pim_...).
2. In the sidebar/dashboard, find Gas Manager (or "Sponsorship Policies" — Pimlico's naming has varied).
3. Click Create Policy.
4. Configure it. Sensible starting values for one agent:
- Name: anything, e.g. merrymen-rex
- Chain: Robinhood Chain (4663) — policies are per-chain
- Daily gas limit / per-userOp limits: generous defaults are fine (e.g. a few USD/day)
- Leave allowlists empty unless you want to restrict which senders can use it (you can add your smart account 0xa48c... to be strict)
5. Save, then deposit funds into the policy — Pimlico requires you to pre-fund the policy with ETH on that chain. Something like 0.01–0.02 ETH covers a lot of sponsored ops at this chain's gas prices (each op costs ~0.0005–0.002).
6. Copy the policy ID (looks like pol_... or a uuid — the dashboard shows it on the policy page).

### Step 2 — Set the two settings

Open your web app → Settings page (http://localhost:3100/settings), or edit the file directly.

Via the file (~/.merrymen/settings.json), add:

"sponsorGasEnabled": true,
"sponsorshipPolicyId": "<your-policy-id>"


Via the Settings UI: there's a sponsored-gas toggle; the policy ID field appears alongside it. Either way, save.

The worker re-reads settings every tick (~60s), but the executor is only rebuilt when the connection fingerprint changes — connectionKey() includes sponsorGasEnabled and sponsorshipPolicyId, so you'll see this in the log:

[worker] executor live — smart account 0xa48c... · SPONSORED gas


(or similar — the "self-paying gas" suffix changes). If it doesn't rebuild, restart npm start.

### Step 3 — Watch it work

Next tick with auto-convert on and your 0.00449 ETH balance:

[auto-convert] account undeployed — deployment is gas-sponsored, deploying at any balance
[executor] gas estimate received
[executor] UserOperation accepted: 0x...
[auto-convert] account deployed=true — proceeding with the convert
[auto-convert] economics: sponsored=true ... surplus=...


Your full balance minus only the small percentage reserve converts to USDG — no deployment top-up needed.

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Meaning |
|---|---|
| the gas sponsor did not answer | Wrong policy ID, or policy on the wrong chain (must be 4663) |
| the gas sponsor declined this operation | Policy out of funds, or policy restricts this sender — check the Pimlico dashboard |
| Sponsor errors but you wanted self-pay anyway | Set sponsorGasEnabled: false — everything falls back to the reserve/pre-check path |

If sponsorship refuses for any reason, nothing is broadcast and nothing is lost — the worker logs it and retries next window.

Let me untangle this — the confusion is understandable because three different things share one API key.

## 1. Will 0.01 ETH work WITHOUT the sponsor?

Yes. With the code that's already pushed:

- Deploy probe costs ~0.0045 ETH of gas (one time)
- Convert then runs with the ~2M-gas floor
- On 0.01 ETH: ~0.0045 for setup, ~0.004 converts to ~10 USDG, rest stays as reserve

Your account is stranded *only because 0.00449 is a hair under the 0.0046 setup cost*. Add 0.01 total and everything works with no sponsor, no policy, nothing extra. Just restart and watch.

## 2. Why doesn't the Pimlico API key alone enable sponsorship?

Because the bundler and the paymaster are different services, even at Pimlico:

| Service | What it does | What it needs |
|---|---|---|
| Bundler | Submits your UserOperation to the chain | Just the API key — you have this ✅ |
| Paymaster | *Pays the gas* from a prepaid deposit | API key + a sponsorship policy you create and fund yourself ❌ |

Your API key makes the bundler work — that's why ops get as far as gas estimation. But "who pays" is a separate contract with a separate prepaid balance. Pimlico will not sponsor ops on an API key alone because someone has to own that gas cost — that's what the policy is. It's not a merrymen limitation; it's how Pimlico's gas manager works.

So: sponsor = optional convenience, not a requirement. The requirement is just: account balance must cover the one-time deployment (~0.005 ETH).

## 3. So what's the actual user experience for "deposit then auto-convert"?

With everything now in the branch:

| First deposit | What happens |
|---|---|
| ≥ ~0.005 ETH | Deploys + converts automatically. Done. |
| < ~0.005 ETH | Funds sit safely on-chain. Worker posts a clear event: *"needs ~X more ETH for one-time setup."* The moment cumulative deposits cross the line, it deploys and converts — original deposit included. |

Nothing is lost in any case. The only wart is the < 0.005 user must send a second deposit. That's the wart the sponsor option removes (hosted users never see it).

## 4. Can there be a manual "Convert now" button?

Yes — the plumbing already exists. The app already queues dashboard commands to the worker (runQueuedCommand runs every tick; /api/selftest writes command files the worker picks up). A manual convert button would:

1. POST /api/convert → writes a queued command file
2. Worker's next tick reads it, runs the exact convert path (with or without sponsor)
3. Result lands in the ledger/events like any auto-convert

That's a genuinely good feature to propose — it gives users a visible action instead of "wait for the tick," and it reuses the tested path.

## 5. Yes — users can input their own policy ID

Already supported: sponsorshipPolicyId is a normal setting (Settings UI / settings.json). A self-hosted user creates their own Pimlico policy, funds it, pastes the ID, flips sponsorGasEnabled. The code was built exactly for that — createSponsor({ url, policyId }).

## 6. What to tell the maintainer

Something like:

>
> Shipped: native-input swap via SwapRouter02, deploy-first flow (dust approve deploys the counterfactual Kernel before the convert), reserve sized to the real EntryPoint prefund (swap msg.value + gas in one op), full diagnostics, AA21 root-caused via ledger events.
>
> Finding: an undeployed account's first UserOp has verification gas ×3 (~6.2M gas ≈ 0.0045 ETH at current prices). Deposits below that can't self-deploy — funds are safe but auto-convert can't start. Options on the table:
> 1. Sponsor the deploy probe via the existing paymaster (sponsorGasEnabled + Pimlico policy) — works at any deposit size; hosted tenants already have the house paymaster, so this is effectively a self-hosted-only gap.
> 2. Manual "Convert now" button via the existing queued-command channel — gives users a visible action.
> 3. Minimum-first-deposit messaging in the fund step.
>
> Tests: 1,584 passing; AA21 path reproducible and fixed in 8a35455, 871c899, 7424a6f + local sponsor-aware/pre-check changes not yet pushed.

## Bottom line for you right now

Simplest path, no sponsor needed: send ~0.005 more ETH to the same account (→ ~0.01 total), restart, done. The sponsor wiring is there if you ever want gas-free ops, and a manual-convert button is a small, high-value feature to propose upstream.

The deploy op's raw bundler estimate is ~7.77M gas (15.5M is after the executor's 2× headroom). Every earlier symptom now checks out against this one number:

| Observation | Explained by |
|---|---|
| AA21 with 0.00449 ETH | raw estimate 7.77M × 0.704 gwei ≈ 0.00547 ETH — just above your balance |

| Today's gas-absurd | the executor's safety ceiling refuses any op over 3M gas — so the deploy op is refused before submission, at any balance |

So: deployment on this chain genuinely costs ~7.8M gas of verification (Kernel v3.3 + validators + factory). It's not your account, not the wall, not the convert — it's that the executor's safety policy (3M ceiling, 2× headroom) cannot express a deployment op at all. The headroom inflation is also what pushes the prefund past your balance: the EntryPoint must prefund the *inflated* limits.

## The fix (plan)

1. Let the executor accept per-call gas bounds. boundGas() already takes a bounds parameter — expose it as an option on execute() so the deploy probe can pass relaxed bounds.
2. Probe op uses headroom 1.2×, ceiling 20M. Deployment is a fixed factory computation — not a swap — so the estimate is stable and the aggressive 2× headroom (designed for swap-estimate jitter) is unnecessary. Bounded op ≈ 9.3M gas → prefund ≈ 0.0066 ETH. Your 0.01028 balance clears it with ~0.0037 left.
3. Convert keeps the existing strict bounds (3M ceiling, 2× headroom) — deployed-account swap ops are well under the ceiling, so the safety policy stays exactly as strict where it matters.
4. Keep everything else: sponsor awareness, pre-check message, diagnostics.

Now I can see the full mechanism, and it's a real (separate) bug worth fixing — here's the honest picture.

## Why it's stuck

The startup reconcile scans for orphaned UserOperations across a 200,000-block range using a span-halving strategy: when a range query fails, it halves and retries — down to single blocks. Your public RPC is rate-limiting (Too Many Requests on every call), so:

full range → 429 → half → 429 → ... → single-block calls → 429 → skip → next block


It's now crawling through up to 200k blocks one-by-one with 429 backoff. That scan runs before the first tick completes — which is why no heartbeat, no [tick], no [account], and no auto-convert. The auto-convert fix is loaded and fine; it's stuck in the queue behind a scan that may take a very long time under throttling.

Your repeated restarts made this worse each time — every restart re-runs the same scan against an already-annoyed RPC.

## Your two options

### Option 1 — wait it out (zero effort, unknown duration)
The scan skips failing blocks and will eventually finish, then the tick runs and the deploy+convert fires. Could be minutes, could be an hour+ depending on how long the RPC throttle lasts. Leave the worker alone and watch for [tick] lines.

### Option 2 — fix the real bug (code change, needs act mode)
The reconcile has no time budget. The correct fix is to time-box it: give the scan a hard budget (e.g. 60–90 seconds); if it can't finish under rate limiting, log a clear warn event ("reconcile skipped — RPC rate-limited; orphan check will retry next arm") and proceed to the first tick. The reconcile's purpose is protecting the daily cap after an unclean restart — a delayed check is the safe direction, whereas blocking the whole worker forever is the unsafe one. That's a ~15-line change in worker/src/index.ts around the reconcile call, plus it makes every future restart immune to this.

My recommendation: Option 2, since you'll hit this on every restart until it's fixed.

## The plan

1. Wrap the arm-time reconcile in a time budget (90s). On expiry: warn event, proceed with tick. (Next arm retries the check — the safety intent is preserved.)
2. Keep everything else untouched.
3. Typecheck + full suite.
4. Then restart → first tick completes immediately → deploy probe (relaxed bounds) → convert.

Switch to act mode and I'll implement it. No commits/pushes until you've seen the conversion land and give the word.

## The one-time deployment fee, explained

### Why it exists

Your agent's smart account is counterfactual — it has an address from the moment you create it, but no code lives there yet. Nothing is on-chain until the first operation pays to actually deploy it.

That first operation has to do everything at once:

1. Deploy the Kernel v3.3 account contract through its factory.
2. Enable the sudo validator (your owner key's control).
3. Enable the permission validator (the session key + the entire call-policy wall).
4. Then execute the actual call (in this case, the dust approve).

And ERC-4337 makes it worse: for an undeployed account, the EntryPoint counts the verification gas ×3 as insurance. That's how a ~7.8M-gas operation becomes a ~0.008 ETH bill at 0.63 gwei.

### What you actually paid

0.010277 ETH  (balance before)
0.008  ETH    ← one-time deployment (spent once, never again)
0.000988 ETH  → converted to 2.42 USDG
0.001272 ETH  (remaining gas, for future ops)


### Why it's strictly one-time

After deployment, the account has code. Every future operation skips steps 1–3 entirely — it's a plain deployed account doing a swap. From now on the cost of converting ETH is just normal swap gas, roughly 0.001–0.002 ETH worth of reserve instead of 0.008. Your second conversion (already visible in the logs' economics lines) will show a much smaller gap between balance and surplus.

### Who it affects

- Every new account, exactly once — this is not specific to auto-convert or your setup. Any first UserOperation (a trade, a vault deposit, an approve) would have paid it.
- Self-hosted users without a paymaster pay it from their own balance — which is why deposits under ~0.005 ETH couldn't deploy at all (the bug we just fixed).
- Hosted users / sponsored ops never see it as a balance requirement — the paymaster's deposit covers the gas, so even a $5 first deposit works.

### Why the UI should say this upfront

The current fund step just says "send ETH." It should say: *"First deposit pays a one-time account setup fee of roughly 0.005–0.01 ETH. After that, any amount works."* That's one of the follow-ups I'd flag to the maintainer — it's the difference between a user thinking the product is broken and a user understanding their money is safe and waiting.

### One reassurance

Even if deployment had failed mid-way, your funds were never at risk — they sat in the counterfactual account, recoverable at any time with the owner key (merrymen recover). The fee is only paid when deployment *succeeds*, and it succeeded.

## What is the one-time deployment fee?

Every merrymen account is counterfactual. When an owner signs a grant at /grant, the smart-account address is *derived* (owner key → sudo validator → factory), but no contract is deployed. The account has an address and can receive funds, but it has no code — it cannot execute anything until its first UserOperation pays to deploy it.

That first UserOperation does four things in one bundle:

1. Deploys the Kernel v3.3 account contract via the factory (createAccount).
2. Enables the sudo validator (the owner key's control).
3. Enables the session-key permission validator — which validates the entire call-policy wall (WALL_POLICY_FLAG, the enable data the owner signed).
4. Executes the actual call (an approve, a swap, whatever the op is).

Two things make this expensive:

- Kernel v3.3 + validator enablement is heavy verification work — Pimlico's live simulation of a real deploy op measured ~7.8M gas raw (this is *before* any swap work; the dust-approve probe costs almost nothing itself).
- ERC-4337 charges verification gas ×3 for undeployed senders. The EntryPoint insures itself against the account failing mid-deployment, so the prefund requirement is computed on 3× the verification estimate.

Measured end-to-end on chain 4663 at ~0.63 gwei:

raw estimate:        ~7.8M gas
bounded (1.2x):      ~9.4M gas   ← what the EntryPoint must prefund
actual cost paid:    ~0.008 ETH  (gas USED, the unspent prefund is refunded)


Verified live: a 0.010277 ETH balance → deploy op → 0.008 ETH spent → account permanently deployed → subsequent convert ran at normal deployed-account cost.

### Why it matters for the product

- It's once per account, ever. After deployment, every op is a plain deployed-account op (~2M-gas floor, pennies at this gas price).
- Deposits below ~0.005 ETH could not self-deploy — AA21 "didn't pay prefund" on every attempt, funds stranded (safe, recoverable, but inert). This was the bug behind "auto-convert doesn't work": the reserve/ceilings were tuned for *swap* ops (3M ceiling, 2× headroom) and can't physically express a 7.8M deployment estimate. Fixed by sizing the deploy probe's bounds to the measured estimate and deploying first with a policy-legal dust approve.
- Hosted tenants never feel it — the house paymaster covers the gas, so any first deposit works. It's a self-hosted-only gap unless a sponsor is configured.
- The UI doesn't warn about it. The fund step should say: *"First operation pays a one-time setup cost of roughly 0.005–0.01 ETH. After that, any amount works."* Without that sentence, a small depositor reads AA21 as a product bug.

---

Worth phrasing it that way, because "fee" implies it went to someone; it went to the chain's validators for ~12M gas of execution.

## Item 2 — updated PR description (copy-paste ready)

---

# Add guarded native ETH → USDG auto-conversion

## Summary

Adds an opt-in flow that converts surplus native ETH to USDG through Uniswap SwapRouter02, keeping a gas reserve. Uses the existing smart account, owner key, and session-key wall — no new wallet, no fund movement.

Live-tested end-to-end: deploy op accepted → account deployed → convert landed → USDG in the ledger and on-chain.

## What changed

### Conversion flow

- One native-input exactInputSingle call: ETH as msg.value, WETH as the router's input token — no separate wrap, no approve for the swap itself.
- Deploy-first: a counterfactual account's first op is a policy-legal dust approve (USDG.approve(router, 1n)) that deploys the Kernel account before the convert runs.
- Reserve sized to the *real* EntryPoint prefund — the swap's msg.value and gas leave the account in the same operation. Floors: 2M gas deployed, 5M undeployed fallback.
- Deploy probe uses per-call gas bounds (1.2× headroom, 20M ceiling) sized to the measured deployment estimate (~7.8M raw gas). Default executor bounds (2×, 3M) are untouched for every other op.
- Hourly cooldown on success; failing ops retry without consuming it.
- In-flight guard prevents duplicate submissions with the same account nonce; 120s execution timeout; 30s bundler-call timeouts; onSubmitted logs the hash before receipt wait.

### Sponsor awareness

- With sponsorGasEnabled + a Pimlico policy, the deploy probe runs sponsored (AA21 can't fire at any balance) and the convert's gas floor shrinks to a drift margin, since gas leaves the paymaster's deposit rather than the account.
- Unsponsored: unchanged self-pay path with a plain-language pre-check.

### Owner-facing behavior

- Deposits below the one-time deployment cost produce a single clear event with the exact top-up amount, instead of an hourly AA21 refusal.
- Full [auto-convert] / [executor] phase logging for every decision.

### Pricing

- Dedicated WETH/USDG execution quote: 15-min TWAP preferred, current spot fallback for freshly initialized pools. Portfolio valuation keeps the strict TWAP-only path.

## The deployment cost finding

An undeployed Kernel v3.3 account's first op simulates at ~7.8M gas (factory + sudo validator + permission-wall enable, verification ×3 by the EntryPoint) ≈ 0.008 ETH spent on chain 4663 — measured live, once per account, ever. Three consequences baked into this PR:

1. Deploy-first flow with per-call bounds (above).
2. A funding pre-check that names the exact shortfall instead of an hourly opaque refusal.
3. Sponsor path removes the balance requirement entirely where a paymaster exists.

## Security

- Swap restricted to the approved router, exactInputSingle, allowlisted tokens, recipient = own account, sealed per-op native value limit.
- No arbitrary ETH transfer or withdrawal permissions; conversion cannot exceed the wall.
- Gas-bounds relaxation applies to the deploy probe only; trade ops keep the strict 3M/2× policy.

## Migration

Same wallet, same smart account, same funds. Re-sign the grant at /grant (old grants predate the native-swap permission), verify the preview address is unchanged, enable auto-convert in Settings.

## Testing

1,584 tests passing; typecheck (worker/web/browser) and production build green. Live verification: deploy op 0xbabbd230… accepted, convert 0x73ae1952… landed (0.000988 ETH → 2.4216 USDG min 2.39631), balances confirmed on-chain.

## Follow-ups (separate issues)

1. Reconcile scan has no time budget — a rate-limited RPC blocks the first tick for many minutes.
2. Ledger records the quoted USDG instead of the actual fill from receipt logs.
3. Fund-step copy should surface the one-time setup cost (~0.008 ETH measured).

---

## Item 3 — three issue drafts (paste into GitHub)

Issue 1 — Reconcile scan blocks the first tick under RPC rate limiting
> At arm, the orphan-op reconcile scans up to 200k blocks with span-halving getLogs. Under public-RPC 429s it degrades to per-block calls and can block the first tick for 30+ minutes (heartbeat stale, no ticks, auto-convert/trading all queued behind it). Observed live on chain 4663. Proposal: time-box the scan (e.g. 90s), emit a warn event on expiry, and retry next arm — a delayed orphan check is the safe direction; a worker that can't start is not.

Issue 2 — Ledger books the quoted USDG, not the actual fill
> auto-convert writes amount_usdg: usdgNum(expect6) — the pre-trade quote — with status: "landed". The receipt's logs carry the real swap output and the repo already has the fills machinery for trades. Conversions should decode the USDG Transfer from ExecutionResult.logs and book the actual amount (falls back to the quote only if logs are unreadable, with basis_source marking it).

Issue 3 — Surface the one-time deployment cost in the fund step
> A counterfactual account's first UserOperation deploys Kernel v3.3 + validators: measured ~7.8M gas ≈ 0.008 ETH on chain 4663, once per account. Deposits below ~0.005 ETH can't self-deploy (AA21) — funds are safe but inert, and the refusal reads like a bug. The fund step should say: "First operation pays a one-time setup cost of roughly 0.005–0.01 ETH; after that, any amount works." Hosted/sponsored users are unaffected.

---

That's all three items done: pushed (d11e731), PR text updated to match reality, and issues drafted. Want me to also draft the maintainer message combining your live test story with the findings?

## Follow-up: live end-to-end verification (funded test on chain 4663)

Tested the full flow with real funds after the fixes in 8a35455 → d11e731. Result: conversion landed and verified on-chain.

### What was run

Self-hosted install, existing smart account 0xa48c…3e75, steady-basket strategy, no paymaster (self-paying gas), auto-convert enabled in Settings, freshly re-signed grant carrying native-swap.

### The debugging trail (worth keeping, it's why the fixes look the way they do)

The initial "it doesn't work" turned out to be four stacked failures, each masking the next:

1. Old grant — signed before native-swap existed; the wall refused native value. Fixed by re-signing (marker minted with the permission, lockstep).
2. Stale quote path — the converter reused the TWAP-based valuation oracle, which refuses fresh pools with no observation history. Fixed with the dedicated execution quote (spot fallback), 1fe179c.
3. AA21 "didn't pay prefund" — the EntryPoint requires the swap's msg.value and the gas prefund to fit in the balance *of the same operation*. Three floors (400k, 1M, 2.5M gas) all undershot; each failure was only diagnosable after surfacing the bundler's actual simulation error from the ledger events — "gas estimate unavailable" alone was useless.
4. The deployment op itself — once AA21 was finally cleared by funding, the executor's gas-absurd ceiling (3M, tuned for swaps) refused the deploy op: Pimlico's simulation of the real deployment measured ~7.8M gas raw (15.5M at 2× headroom). Fixed with per-call bounds on the deploy probe only (d11e731).

## Follow-up: live testing found four stacked bugs — all fixed and pushed to this branch

After opening this PR I ran it against a funded live account on chain 4663 (self-hosted, self-paying gas, no paymaster). The feature didn't fire — and peeling that apart surfaced four separate failures, each masking the next. All are fixed in commits now pushed to this branch.

The converter reused the TWAP-based *valuation* oracle, which refuses pools without observation history — exactly the state a first conversion can hit. Added a dedicated execution quote for the convert path only: TWAP preferred, current spot fallback otherwise. Portfolio valuation keeps the strict TWAP-only behavior.

### 2. The reserve ignored that the swap value and gas leave together (8a35455)

The EntryPoint's AA21 check needs the account to cover the swap's msg.value and the gas prefund in the *same* operation. The original reserve budgeted gas only, so the converter always tried to spend ~90% of the balance and the simulation found nothing left to prefund with. Floors are now sized to the real op shape.

### 3. The deployment op physically cannot pass swap-tuned bounds (d11e731)

With funding increased, the next refusal was the executor's own gas-absurd ceiling (3M gas, 2× headroom). Pimlico's simulation of a real deployment op measured ~7.8M gas raw — Kernel v3.3 + sudo validator + permission-wall enable, with the EntryPoint counting verification ×3. A deploy op can *never* fit swap bounds, at any balance. The executor now accepts per-call bounds; the deploy probe uses 1.2× headroom / 20M ceiling (deployment is fixed factory calldata — no estimate jitter). Every other op keeps the strict defaults unchanged.

### 4. The deploy happens first now (7424a6f)

A counterfactual account is deployed by a policy-legal dust approve (USDG.approve(router, 1n)) before the convert runs, so the convert itself is always a cheap deployed-account op. And when the balance can't cover the one-time deployment (~0.008 ETH measured), the owner now gets one clear event naming the exact top-up instead of an hourly opaque refusal. Sponsorship path included: with sponsorGasEnabled, the probe runs sponsored and works at any balance.

Three paste-ready issues, one per item:

---

### Issue 1

Title: Arm-time reconcile scan can stall the first tick for 30+ minutes under rate-limited RPC

Body:

At arm, the orphan-op reconcile scans EntryPoint UserOperationEvent logs over up to 200,000 blocks using a span-halving getLogs strategy (worker/src/inflight-reconcile.ts). When the RPC rate-limits, the span halves down to per-block calls, each subject to 429 backoff. The scan runs before the first tick completes — heartbeat goes stale, no [tick]/[account] lines, and trading plus auto-convert are all queued behind it.

Observed live on chain 4663 (self-hosted, public RPC rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com): repeated Too Many Requests on single-block queries, first tick blocked for 30+ minutes across restarts. Every restart re-runs the same scan, making it worse.

Why it's the unsafe direction: the reconcile exists to protect the daily cap after an unclean restart — but a worker that can't *start* protects nothing and looks broken. A delayed orphan check is safe; a blocked worker is not.

Proposal: time-box the scan (e.g. 90 seconds at arm). On expiry, emit a warn event ("reconcile incomplete — RPC rate-limited; orphan check retried next arm") and proceed to the first tick. The next arm retries the check, so the safety intent survives; optionally persist scan progress so the retry resumes rather than restarts.

---

### Issue 2

Title: Auto-convert ledger row books the pre-trade quote instead of the actual fill

Body:

worker/src/index.ts (auto-convert success path) writes:

amount_usdg: usdgNum(expect6),   // the quote, not the fill
status: "landed",


expect6 is the pre-trade estimate from the pool price. The receipt's logs carry the actual USDG transferred, and the repo already has the machinery to decode it — netTokenDeltas/fills.ts, used by every trade intent via ExecutionResult.logs.

Impact: the ledger's P&L, equity and basis records for conversions are estimates presented as settled facts — the exact thing fills.ts exists to prevent for trades (basis_source exists precisely to distinguish the two).

Proposal: decode the USDG Transfer leg from ExecutionResult.logs for the convert op; book the actual amount with basis_source: "receipt", falling back to the quote only if the logs are unreadable — and mark that fallback explicitly, same discipline as trades.

---

### Issue 3

Title: Fund step should warn about the one-time account deployment cost

Body:

A counterfactual account's first UserOperation deploys Kernel v3.3 + sudo validator + the permission wall's validator enable, all inside one op, with the EntryPoint counting verification gas ×3. Measured live on chain 4663: ~7.8M gas raw ≈ 0.008 ETH actually spent (prefund remainder refunded by the EntryPoint). Once per account, ever — after it, every op is a cheap deployed-account op.

User impact: deposits below ~0.005 ETH cannot self-deploy — the bundler refuses with AA21 "didn't pay prefund" on every attempt. Funds are safe and recoverable (merrymen recover), but inert, and the refusal reads like a product bug. Auto-convert's pre-check now emits a clear "needs ~X more ETH for one-time setup" event (see PR), but the fund step itself still says only "send ETH."

Proposal: the onboarding fund step (and /grant funding copy) states: *"The first operation pays a one-time account setup cost of roughly 0.005–0.01 ETH. After that, any amount works."* Hosted/sponsored users are unaffected (the house paymaster covers it), so the copy can be conditional on sponsorGasEnabled.

---

Adjust tone or trim as you like — each is self-contained with its measured evidence, so the maintainer can triage without re-deriving the investigation.

Fetched the upstream repo. Before creating anything, here's an honest review of the four ideas against what actually exists in the codebase — because two of them are natural extensions, and two of them quietly break the product's core promise. The maintainer will see that immediately, so the PR needs to address it head-on.

## Review of the four ideas

### 1. Cash wallet → cross-chain trade execution

What exists: the smart-account architecture (Kernel/ERC-4337) is chain-agnostic in principle; the hosted-worker-design doc already sketches "cross-chain intent execution" as a gap (§2.3, insertion points in packages/core/src/chain.ts). But the entire venue/token/route layer (STOCK_TOKENS, UNISWAP, CASH) is hard-pinned to chains 4663/46630. The grant/wall is deployed per-chain.

Gap: bridges or an intent/settlement layer, multi-chain registry, per-chain grants, and a cash-in/cash-out UX. This is the biggest lift by far — realistically its own project, not a PR.

Verdict: right long-term direction, wrong first PR. Stage it.

### 2. Sign up with X → wallet created → top up

What exists: the auth layer already does wallet-based sign-in (SIWE-style challenge → session cookie, web/src/lib/auth.ts, /api/auth/session). Hosted mode already creates and stores per-tenant state (grant-store, settings-store). So "sign in → provisioned account" exists — just with a wallet instead of X.

The problem: "get your cross-chain wallet created" means the service generates/custodies keys. That directly contradicts the repo's headline promise — *"your keys never leave your machine… enforced on-chain, not by promises"* — and the README even calls out that TEE custody is explicitly not shipped. A maintainer who wrote that will reject embedded custody unless it's architected as non-custodial (passkey/session-key model, or an MPC/TEE design that's honestly labeled as a custody-model change).

Verdict: feasible as "sign in with X links your existing non-custodial agent account" (X as identity, wallet stays user-generated). Wallet-*creation*-for-you needs a design conversation first, not code.

### 3. Watch other bots + live leaderboard with PnL before creating your own

What exists: /scoreboard already ships — public leaderboard reading real ledger data. The hosted ledger (Postgres, multi-tenant) already aggregates per-agent financials (getAgentFinancials, HWM, realized PnL). A "watch live bots" feed is a read-only view over existing tables.

Gap: anonymity/consent (publishing users' PnL needs opt-in), and "live" streaming (the current feed is poll-based).

Verdict: easiest win, do this first. Mostly web/UI work over existing data. Great first PR: extend /scoreboard with live PnL, bot cards, and an opt-in "show my bot" toggle.

### 4. Bot creation flow: name → strategy → launch

What exists: almost all of it. Agent naming (soul.ts, setName), strategy selection (builtin + custom, /settings), the muster flow (Onboarding.tsx — connect/create/fund steps), hosted auto-arm. The grant flow already caps per-trade/daily/expiry at creation.

Gap: it's currently spread across /app onboarding + /grant + /settings — the idea is to collapse it into one linear "create bot" wizard. That's a UX reorganization, not new infrastructure.

Verdict: second PR — genuinely valuable and mostly presentational.

## Recommended PR strategy

Don't open one mega-PR — open a proposal issue on upstream with this roadmap, then land PRs in this order:

| Order | PR | Effort | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Live leaderboard + watch-bots view (extend /scoreboard, opt-in PnL) | ~days | low |
| 2 | Unified "create your bot" wizard (name → strategy → caps → launch) | ~1–2 weeks | low |
| 3 | X sign-in as identity linking (wallet stays non-custodial) | ~2 weeks | medium |
| 4 | Cross-chain execution (design doc first, then intent layer) | months | high |

Ordering matters: 1 and 2 make the product demo-able to new users *before* the custody/cross-chain conversations; 3 needs maintainer buy-in on the custody stance; 4 needs a design doc (docs/) before any code, same as the hosted-worker design.

## The framing that gets this merged

Lead the proposal with what *doesn't* change: non-custodial keys, on-chain caps, the wall. Every feature above can be built without touching custody — except the literal "we create your wallet," which should be reframed as *"we provision your agent; you hold the key"* (the current browser-generated key model, just with X as the login).

Want me to draft the proposal issue text + the PR-1 (leaderboard/watch-bots) implementation plan next? Or if you want, I can start scaffolding PR-1 on a new branch off upstream/main.
